riskAssessment.reason: The main risk is allowing downstream code to mistake a supplied Distance value for a locally calculated judgment, or to lose evidence identity/order while building a read-only per-company boundary.
riskAssessment.reviewNotes: The Distance formula is intentionally not provided and is not guessed; this WI receives Distance as an explicit upstream-supplied value. WR-004 owns transition output, WR-007 owns compression, and later WIs own persistence/rendering/delivery.

reasons: Typed Domain boundary, tests, documentation, and governance evidence require the standard governed review route.

executionDecision.reason: The explicit user authorization covers execution and Contract recording for all 24 roadmap Work Items, and the supplied-value boundary is codable without guessing a Distance formula.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: ThresholdDistance exposes exactly four supplied Distance variants with stable labels FAR, DEVELOPING, NEAR, and CANDIDATE.
ThresholdDistance retains the supplied company reference, current_stage, next_stage, confirmed evidence order, missing evidence order, and Distance value through public accessors.
Construction accepts Distance as an explicit upstream value and contains no formula, threshold comparison, Stage inference, Transition detection, score calculation, or evidence conclusion logic.
Construction rejects blank company/stage/evidence values and rejects empty confirmed or missing evidence collections with deterministic domain errors.
Construction rejects duplicate evidence identities within either collection and rejects any identity appearing in both confirmed and missing evidence collections.

The implementation is standalone standard-library Domain code and does not modify or import the shared Weekly Radar modules, architecture guard, persistence, renderer, Telegram, Scheduler, or another Work Item.

Focused unit and integration tests plus the design spec and execution plan cover supplied-value retention, four Distance labels, ordering, blank input, duplicate evidence, overlap rejection, no-formula behavior, authorization, and current-WI issue handling.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Threshold Distance receives Distance as an upstream-supplied value; never guess or implement a Distance formula in this WI.
Preserve current_stage, next_stage, confirmed evidence, missing evidence, Distance, evidence identity, and collection order exactly as supplied.
Reject blank values, duplicate evidence identities, and Confirmed/Missing evidence overlap deterministically.
Keep this source standalone and independent of shared Weekly Radar modules, other feature implementations, persistence, rendering, Telegram, Scheduler, and external runtime dependencies.
Do not add dependencies for this Contract.
Resolve issues within the current Work Item when they remain inside its Contract scope; open a successor only for a distinct or materially expanded boundary.
Do not introduce trading, price prediction, target price, portfolio allocation, or capital-action behavior.

intent.problem: Weekly Radar needs a typed per-company Threshold Distance read-only boundary, but the repository must not silently invent a Far/Developing/Near/Candidate formula or lose the evidence lists that explain the supplied value.
constraints: Receive Distance as an explicit upstream-supplied value because no authoritative Distance formula is provided; retain it without inference or recalculation.
Retain current_stage, next_stage, confirmed evidence, and missing evidence in input order, while rejecting blank values, duplicate evidence identities, and Confirmed/Missing overlap.
Write only the exclusive threshold_distance.rs, its integration test, dedicated docs, and this WI's governed evidence; do not modify shared Weekly Radar module files or other Work Items.
intent.rationale: A small standalone read-only boundary gives later Weekly Radar assembly and rendering WIs a deterministic container while keeping stage semantics, evidence judgment, persistence, and delivery in their owning boundaries.
